European Sovereign Green Bond Event Study¶

Thesis: When Governments Say Green - Do Bond Markets Believe Them? Author: Nahian Ibnat | Supervisor: Zoltan Csaba Toth Institution: Central European University | Date: May 2026

Role of this notebook¶

This notebook implements the event study for Germany and Denmark - the comparative European extension. Asia produced null H3 results. Europe tests whether the same methodology detects greeniums in deeper, more liquid markets.

Critical economic corrections from the prior draft¶

Issue What was wrong Fix
Germany pre-event weeks misinterpreted Described as parallel trends test, but green bond did not exist before treatment date Reframed as post-issuance price discovery, not parallel trends
Denmark same problem Conventional twin exists pre-issuance but green bond does not - no pre-treatment greenium Acknowledged; parallel trends for Denmark comes from stacked DiD Stack A
Pooled event study limitation undocumented Germany and Denmark combined with no warning about conflation of different macro periods Explicit warning added
Summary false positive Any significant week counted as treatment detected Fixed
No formal test Pre-trend assessed visually Joint F-test on post-event dummies added
FX/CDS not forward-filled Weekend gaps silently dropped Added

Critical economic insight - why Europe is different from Asia¶

In Asia, India has a genuine pre-treatment window of ~120 trading days because the second auction treatment event (Oct 2023) occurs months after the green bond started trading (Jan 2023).

In Europe, BOTH Germany and Denmark issued green bonds FOR THE FIRST TIME at the treatment date. The greenium cannot exist before the green bond exists. Therefore:

  • There is NO genuine pre-treatment greenium data for Germany or Denmark
  • The event study documents POST-ISSUANCE dynamics, not a classic DiD
  • Parallel trends for Europe is validated by the stacked DiD (regression notebook)
  • The event study here shows how quickly and persistently the greenium established
Country Pre-treatment greenium data Parallel trends testable here
India YES (~120 trading days) YES
Indonesia Very limited (~55 days) Weakly
Germany NO (bond issued at treatment) NO
Denmark NO (bond issued at treatment) NO

1.4 - Helper functions and chart styling¶

In [4]:
def load_bond_ytm(filepath):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(filepath)
    ws = wb.active
    rows = list(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True))
    hdr_idx = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if r[0] and "date" in str(r[0]).lower())
    df = pd.DataFrame([r for r in rows[hdr_idx+1:] if r[0] is not None], columns=rows[hdr_idx])
    df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"])
    df["ytm"]  = (df["BidYld"] + df["AskYld"]) / 2
    return df[["date","ytm"]].dropna().sort_values("date").reset_index(drop=True)

def load_investing_fx(filepath, col_name):
    df = pd.read_csv(filepath)
    df["date"]   = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"])
    df[col_name] = pd.to_numeric(df["Price"].astype(str).str.replace(",",""), errors="coerce")
    return df[["date", col_name]].dropna().sort_values("date").reset_index(drop=True)

def load_cds(filepath, col_name):
    df = pd.read_csv(filepath)
    df.columns = ["date", col_name, "open", "high", "low", "chg"]
    df["date"]   = pd.to_datetime(df["date"])
    df[col_name] = pd.to_numeric(df[col_name], errors="coerce")
    return df[["date", col_name]].dropna().sort_values("date").reset_index(drop=True)

def style_ax(ax):
    ax.set_facecolor('white')
    ax.tick_params(colors='#222222', labelsize=8)
    ax.xaxis.label.set_color('#222222'); ax.yaxis.label.set_color('#222222')
    ax.title.set_color('#222222')
    for s in ax.spines.values(): s.set_edgecolor('#cccccc')
    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False); ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

Part 2 - Data Loading and Panel Construction¶

2.1 - Bond yields and greenium¶

Both European pairs are exact twins: identical coupon (0%), identical maturity date, same sovereign issuer. The greenium is a model-free pure green label premium.

In [5]:
bond_dfs = {}
for key, fpath in BOND_FILES.items():
    bond_dfs[key] = load_bond_ytm(fpath)

panels = []
for gkey, ckey, country, tenor in PAIRS:
    g = bond_dfs[gkey].rename(columns={"ytm":"ytm_green"})
    c = bond_dfs[ckey].rename(columns={"ytm":"ytm_conv"})
    m = pd.merge(g, c, on="date", how="inner")
    m["greenium"] = m["ytm_green"] - m["ytm_conv"]
    m["country"]  = country
    m["tenor"]    = tenor
    m["pair_id"]  = f"{country}_{tenor}"
    panels.append(m)

panel = pd.concat(panels, ignore_index=True)
print(f"Raw panel: {len(panel):,} obs")
print(panel.groupby(["country","tenor"]).agg(
    obs=("date","count"), start=("date","min"),
    end=("date","max"), mean_greenium=("greenium","mean")
).round(4).to_string())

2.2 - Merge controls¶

In [6]:
vix = pd.read_csv(VIX_FILE)
vix.columns = ["date","vix"]
vix["date"] = pd.to_datetime(vix["date"])
vix = vix[vix["vix"] != "."].copy()
vix["vix"] = pd.to_numeric(vix["vix"])

eurusd = load_investing_fx(EURUSD_FILE, "eurusd")
usddkk = load_investing_fx(USDDKK_FILE, "usddkk")
usddkk["dkkusd"] = 1 / usddkk["usddkk"]
usddkk = usddkk[["date","dkkusd"]]
cds_deu = load_cds(CDS_DEU_FILE, "cds_germany")

sent = pd.read_csv(SENTIMENT_FILE, parse_dates=["date"])
sent_deu = sent[sent["country"]=="Germany"][["date","sentiment_gdelt","sentiment_std"]].copy()
sent_deu.columns = ["date","sentiment","signaling_noise"]
sent_dnk = sent[sent["country"]=="Denmark"][["date","sentiment_gdelt","sentiment_std"]].copy()
sent_dnk.columns = ["date","sentiment","signaling_noise"]

deu_p = panel[panel["country"]=="Germany"].merge(sent_deu, on="date", how="left")
dnk_p = panel[panel["country"]=="Denmark"].merge(sent_dnk, on="date", how="left")
panel = pd.concat([deu_p, dnk_p], ignore_index=True)

vix_ff = (vix.set_index("date")
             .reindex(pd.date_range(panel.date.min(), panel.date.max()))
             .ffill().reset_index())
vix_ff.columns = ["date","vix"]
panel = panel.merge(vix_ff, on="date", how="left")

panel = panel.merge(eurusd, on="date", how="left")
panel = panel.merge(usddkk, on="date", how="left")
panel["fx"] = np.where(panel["country"]=="Germany", panel["eurusd"], panel["dkkusd"])
panel = panel.drop(columns=["eurusd","dkkusd"])

panel = panel.merge(cds_deu, on="date", how="left")
panel["cds"] = panel["cds_germany"]
panel = panel.drop(columns=["cds_germany"])

# Forward-fill FX and CDS gaps within country
panel = panel.sort_values(["pair_id","date"]).reset_index(drop=True)
panel["fx"]  = panel.groupby("country")["fx"].ffill()
panel["cds"] = panel.groupby("country")["cds"].ffill()

panel["log_fx"]  = np.log(panel["fx"].clip(lower=1e-6))
panel["log_vix"] = np.log(panel["vix"].clip(lower=1e-6))

panel = panel.dropna(subset=["sentiment","signaling_noise","vix","cds","fx"]).reset_index(drop=True)
print(f"Panel after merge: {len(panel):,} obs")
print(panel.groupby(["country","tenor"]).agg(obs=("date","count"), start=("date","min"), end=("date","max")).to_string())
print("OK Controls merged. FX and CDS forward-filled.")

2.3 - First-differencing¶

In [7]:
panel = panel.sort_values(["pair_id","date"]).reset_index(drop=True)

for col in ["greenium","sentiment","signaling_noise","log_vix","log_fx","cds"]:
    panel[f"{col}_fd"] = panel.groupby("pair_id")[col].diff()

panel_fd = panel.dropna(subset=["greenium_fd"]).reset_index(drop=True)

for col in ["sentiment_fd","signaling_noise_fd","log_vix_fd","log_fx_fd","cds_fd"]:
    mu = panel_fd[col].mean(); sd = panel_fd[col].std()
    panel_fd[f"{col}_z"] = (panel_fd[col] - mu) / sd if sd > 0 else 0.0

print(f"First-differenced panel: {len(panel_fd):,} obs")
print("NaN check:")
for col in ["greenium_fd","sentiment_fd_z","log_vix_fd_z","cds_fd_z","log_fx_fd_z"]:
    print(f"  {col:<30} NaN={panel_fd[col].isna().sum()}")
print("OK Ready for event study.")

Part 3 - Germany: Post-Issuance Price Discovery¶

Economic framing¶

Germany has NO pre-treatment greenium data. The green Bund (DE0001030708) was issued on 2 Sep 2020. Before that date the bond did not exist. The event study for Germany therefore does NOT test parallel trends in the DiD sense.

What it shows instead: the price discovery dynamic in weeks after inaugural issuance. Did the greenium establish itself immediately, or did it take weeks to settle? This complements the regression results by documenting the temporal pattern, not providing causal identification.

The DiD identification for Germany relies on the twin-bond design (identical coupon 0%, identical maturity Aug 2030) and issuance date exogeneity.

NOTE on pre-event weeks: Week -1 is the week immediately before issuance. Since the green bond started trading AT the issuance date, pre-event weeks have very few or zero observations and should NOT be interpreted as a pre-treatment baseline.

3.1 - Assign event time (Germany)¶

In [8]:
panel_deu_es = panel_fd[panel_fd["country"]=="Germany"].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

treat_date_deu = TREATMENT_DATES["Germany"]
country_dates  = np.sort(panel_deu_es["date"].unique())
treat_idx      = np.searchsorted(country_dates, np.datetime64(treat_date_deu))
date_to_event  = {d: int(i - treat_idx) for i, d in enumerate(country_dates)}
panel_deu_es["event_time"] = panel_deu_es["date"].map(date_to_event)
panel_deu_es["event_week"] = (panel_deu_es["event_time"] / 5).apply(np.floor).astype(int)

WEEK_MIN_DEU, WEEK_MAX_DEU = -5, 20
panel_deu_es = panel_deu_es[panel_deu_es["event_week"].between(WEEK_MIN_DEU, WEEK_MAX_DEU)].copy()

print(f"Germany: {len(panel_deu_es):,} obs | {treat_date_deu.date()} | weeks {WEEK_MIN_DEU} to {WEEK_MAX_DEU}")

for w, n in panel_deu_es.groupby("event_week").size().items():

    print(f"  Week {w:>4}: {n:>3} obs{note}")

3.2 - Germany regression¶

In [9]:
ev_dummies_deu = pd.get_dummies(panel_deu_es["event_week"].astype(str),
                               drop_first=False, dtype=float)
if "-1" in ev_dummies_deu.columns:
    ev_dummies_deu = ev_dummies_deu.drop(columns=["-1"])

panel_deu_reg = pd.concat([panel_deu_es, ev_dummies_deu], axis=1)
ev_cols_deu   = list(ev_dummies_deu.columns)

X_deu     = sm.add_constant(panel_deu_reg[ev_cols_deu])
model_deu = OLS(panel_deu_reg["greenium_fd"], X_deu).fit(cov_type="HC3")
all_weeks_deu = sorted(range(WEEK_MIN_DEU, WEEK_MAX_DEU + 1))
ci_deu = model_deu.conf_int(alpha=0.05)
coefs_deu, lo_deu, hi_deu, p_deu = [], [], [], []

for w in all_weeks_deu:
    col = str(w)
    if col in model_deu.params.index:
        coefs_deu.append(model_deu.params[col])
        lo_deu.append(ci_deu.loc[col, 0])
        hi_deu.append(ci_deu.loc[col, 1])
        p_deu.append(model_deu.pvalues[col])
    else:
        coefs_deu.append(0.0); lo_deu.append(0.0); hi_deu.append(0.0); p_deu.append(1.0)

print(f"Germany: N={int(model_deu.nobs):,}  R2={model_deu.rsquared:.4f}  DW={durbin_watson(model_deu.resid):.4f}")
print("\nGERMANY POST-ISSUANCE PRICE DISCOVERY (not parallel trends)")
print("=" * 70)
print(f"{'Week':<8} {'Period':<10} {'Coef':>10} {'CI Lo':>10} {'CI Hi':>10} {'p':>8} {'Sig'}")
print("-" * 70)
for w, c, lo, hi, p in zip(all_weeks_deu, coefs_deu, lo_deu, hi_deu, p_deu):
    period = "Pre(*)" if w < -1 else "Ref   " if w == -1 else "Post  "
    ref    = "(ref)" if w == -1 else ("***" if p<0.01 else "**" if p<0.05 else "*" if p<0.1 else "")
    print(f"{w:<8} {period:<10} {c:>+10.4f} {lo:>10.4f} {hi:>10.4f} {p:>8.4f} {ref}")
print("\n(*) Pre-event weeks are economically thin. Do NOT interpret as parallel trends.")

Part 4 - Denmark: Post-Issuance Dynamics¶

Economic framing¶

Denmark issued its inaugural green bond on 21 Jan 2022. Like Germany, the green bond did not exist before the issuance date. The pre-event weeks in the event window do not represent a genuine pre-treatment greenium baseline.

The parallel trends assumption for Denmark is validated through Stack A of the stacked DiD in the regression notebook, where Germany (already treated Sep 2020) serves as the control for Denmark issuance in Jan 2022. That is the proper identification validation for Denmark, not this event study.

What this event study shows: how Denmark greenium evolved in the weeks after inaugural issuance. Given that Denmark is described as showing a textbook greenium compression pattern (sharp sustained drop at issuance), the post-event coefficient should show a significant negative level shift.

4.1 - Assign event time (Denmark)¶

In [11]:
panel_dnk_es = panel_fd[panel_fd["country"]=="Denmark"].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

treat_date_dnk = TREATMENT_DATES["Denmark"]
country_dates  = np.sort(panel_dnk_es["date"].unique())
treat_idx      = np.searchsorted(country_dates, np.datetime64(treat_date_dnk))
date_to_event  = {d: int(i - treat_idx) for i, d in enumerate(country_dates)}
panel_dnk_es["event_time"] = panel_dnk_es["date"].map(date_to_event)
panel_dnk_es["event_week"] = (panel_dnk_es["event_time"] / 5).apply(np.floor).astype(int)

WEEK_MIN_DNK, WEEK_MAX_DNK = -10, 20
panel_dnk_es = panel_dnk_es[panel_dnk_es["event_week"].between(WEEK_MIN_DNK, WEEK_MAX_DNK)].copy()

print(f"Denmark: {len(panel_dnk_es):,} obs | {treat_date_dnk.date()} | weeks {WEEK_MIN_DNK} to {WEEK_MAX_DNK}")
pre_obs = (panel_dnk_es["event_week"] < 0).sum()
print(f"Pre-event obs: {pre_obs}  (NOTE: bond did not exist before issuance - thin data)")
for w, n in panel_dnk_es.groupby("event_week").size().items():
    marker = " <- issuance week" if w==0 else " <- reference (omitted)" if w==-1 else ""
    print(f"  Week {w:>4}: {n:>3} obs{marker}")

Part 5 - Pooled Event Study (Germany + Denmark)¶

Limitation note¶

Pooling Germany (treatment Sep 2020) and Denmark (treatment Jan 2022) in one regression imposes the assumption that the greenium dynamic is identical across both events. These events occurred 16 months apart in very different macro environments (post-COVID recovery vs pre-rate-hike). The pooled chart is useful for a thesis overview figure but the country-specific results in Parts 3 and 4 are primary.

5.1 - Pooled event time assignment¶

In [14]:
panel_es = panel_fd.copy()
panel_es["event_time"] = np.nan

for country, treat_date in TREATMENT_DATES.items():
    mask          = panel_es["country"] == country
    country_dates = np.sort(panel_es.loc[mask, "date"].unique())
    treat_idx     = np.searchsorted(country_dates, np.datetime64(treat_date))
    date_to_event = {d: int(i - treat_idx) for i, d in enumerate(country_dates)}
    panel_es.loc[mask, "event_time"] = panel_es.loc[mask, "date"].map(date_to_event)

panel_es["event_week"] = (panel_es["event_time"] / 5).apply(np.floor).astype(int)
WEEK_MIN, WEEK_MAX = -10, 20
panel_es = panel_es[panel_es["event_week"].between(WEEK_MIN, WEEK_MAX)].copy()

Part 7 - Joint F-Test on Post-Event Dummies¶

What we test here¶

Because both countries lack pre-treatment data, we cannot run a parallel trends F-test. Instead we run a joint F-test on post-event dummies to assess whether the post-issuance greenium dynamics are statistically structured (non-random).

H0: All post-event week coefficients = 0 (no systematic post-issuance pattern)

A significant result means the greenium showed a structured dynamic after inaugural issuance. This complements the regression notebook M5 Post coefficient by showing the SHAPE of the post-event response, not just the level shift.

In [18]:
def post_event_joint_test(model, all_weeks, label):
    post_cols = [str(w) for w in all_weeks if w > 0 and str(w) in model.params.index]
    if not post_cols:
        print(f"[{label}] No post-event dummies.")
        return
    wald   = model.wald_test(post_cols, use_f=True)
    f_stat = float(wald.statistic)
    p_val  = float(wald.pvalue)
    result = "SIGNIFICANT: structured post-issuance dynamics" if p_val < 0.1 else              "NOT significant: no systematic post-issuance pattern"
    print(f" \n[{label}]")
    print(f"  Weeks tested: {len(post_cols)} post-event dummies")
    print(f"  Joint F({len(post_cols)}, {int(model.df_resid)}) = {f_stat:.4f}  p = {p_val:.4f}")
    print(f"  Result: {result}")

print("JOINT F-TEST ON POST-EVENT DUMMIES - EUROPE")
print("=" * 65)
print("H0: All post-event coefficients = 0")
print("NOTE: This tests post-issuance dynamics, NOT parallel trends")
print()
post_event_joint_test(model_es,  all_weeks,     "POOLED")
post_event_joint_test(model_deu, all_weeks_deu, "GERMANY")
post_event_joint_test(model_dnk, all_weeks_dnk, "DENMARK")
print()
print("INTERPRETATION:")
print("  Significant -> greenium had structured dynamics after inaugural issuance")
print("  Not significant -> post-event coefficients jointly indistinguishable from zero")
print("  Consistent with M5 Post coefficient from regression notebook?")
print(f"  Check regression notebook M5_Germany and M5_Denmark for comparison")

]:
    post_coefs = [c for w,c in zip(weeks,coefs_) if w > 0]
    post_sig5  = sum(1 for w,p in zip(weeks,pvals_) if w > 0 and p < 0.05)
    post_sig10 = sum(1 for w,p in zip(weeks,pvals_) if w > 0 and p < 0.10)
    mean_post  = sum(post_coefs)/len(post_coefs) if post_coefs else 0
    verdict = "Structured compression" if post_sig5 >= 2 else               "Weak pattern" if post_sig10 >= 1 else "No pattern"
    print(f" \n[{label}]")
    print(f"  Mean post-event beta: {mean_post:+.5f} pp")
    print(f"  Significant post weeks (p<0.05): {post_sig5}/{len(post_coefs)}")
    print(f"  Significant post weeks (p<0.10): {post_sig10}/{len(post_coefs)}")

KEY THESIS IMPLICATIONS
=================================================================

1. PARALLEL TRENDS:
   Cannot be tested from event study for Germany or Denmark.
   Both issued green bonds AT the treatment date.
   Validation comes from stacked DiD Stack A (regression notebook).

2. POST-ISSUANCE DYNAMICS:
   See coefficient tables and charts above.
   Negative significant post-event betas = greenium compression after issuance.

3. COMPARISON WITH ASIA:
   Asia: null H3, no post-event dynamics.
   Europe: check results above.
   If Europe shows systematic compression, this supports market maturity interpretation.
